CVE-2011-10008.title: MPlayer Lite r33064 M3U Stack-Based Buffer Overflow
CVE-2011-10008.description: A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in MPlayer Lite r33064 due to improper bounds checking when handling M3U playlist files containing long http:// URL entries. An attacker can craft a malicious .m3u file with a specially formatted URL that triggers a stack overflow when processed by the player, particularly via drag-and-drop interaction. This flaw allows for control of the execution flow through SEH overwrite and a DEP bypass using a ROP chain that leverages known gadgets in loaded DLLs. Successful exploitation may result in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the current user.

CVE-2026-119282.title: Nx: OS command injection via nx.json plugin options in @nx/maven and @nx/gradle
CVE-2026-119282.description: Nx is a monorepo solution for TypeScript and polyglot codebases. From 22.0.2 until 22.7.9 and 23.1.2 for @nx/maven, and from 21.0.0 until 22.7.9 and 23.1.2 for @nx/gradle, the plugins' project-graph analyzers launch through a shell and interpolate plugin options from nx.json into command arguments. The @nx/maven targetNamePrefix value and arbitrary @nx/gradle option names or values can therefore be interpreted as shell syntax whenever an nx command constructs the project graph. A user who runs Nx in an attacker-controlled repository or pull request can execute injected commands with the user's privileges, while workspaces that register neither affected plugin are not exposed to this path. Remediation requires upgrading both nx and each affected plugin to matching releases because the plugin fix depends on code in the nx package. This issue is fixed in versions 22.7.9 and 23.1.2.

CVE-2026-126068.title: Action Mailbox: Possible signature replay in Action Mailbox Mailgun ingress

CVE-2026-133422.title: Quadratic time unique_items list validation in Pydantic V1
CVE-2026-133422.description:
Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate.

The ConstrainedList.unique_items_validator validator (in pydantic/types.py) checks each item against all the following ones. For a list with no duplicates (the common, valid case), this results in a quadratic number of comparisons.

The issue was fixed in commit 6ec75e57f277a820ec583e601167f25fe8dc7c87. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted lists into fields constrained with unique_items=True (using conlist() or Field()).

The fix only applies to lists of builtin scalar types (int, float, str, bytes, bool and None), for which duplicates can be detected in linear time. Lists of other types (e.g. models or dictionaries) are still checked in…

CVE-2026-134056.title: Out-of-bounds write in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC
CVE-2026-134056.description:
An out-of-bounds write issue exists in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC. It affects applications that decrypt CBC or ECB ciphertext with PKCS7 padding over multiple calls into the minimum documented output buffer. A remote user who supplies crafted ciphertext might crash the application or corrupt adjacent memory. Affected are all versions of AWS-LC before 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.x before 4.2.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 3.x before 3.6.0, and AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x before 2.0.18.

To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS-LC 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.2.0, or AWS-LC-FIPS 3.6.0.

AWS-LC-FIPS 2.0.18 is also fixed; AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x reaches end of support in April 2027.

CVE-2026-99247.title: tracing: Do not initialize tracefs work if tracing is disabled
CVE-2026-99247.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Do not initialize tracefs work if tracing is disabled

If trace buffer allocation fails during early boot (e.g. in
early_trace_init() -> allocate_trace_buffers()), tracing_disabled is
left set to 1 and the global trace array events list remains
uninitialized.

Later during boot, tracer_init_tracefs() (invoked via fs_initcall)
queues tracerfs_init_work asynchronously without checking if tracing was
disabled. When tracer_init_tracefs_work_func() runs, it calls
event_trace_init() and init_tracer_tracefs(&global_trace, NULL)
unconditionally. This leads to __find_event_file() dereferencing an
uninitialized tr->events list, causing an early boot NULL pointer
dereference Oops:

BUG: Kernel NULL pointer dereference on read at 0x00000010
Faulting instruction address: 0xc000000000485be0
Oops: Kernel access of bad area, sig: 7 [#1]
...
NIP [c000000000485be0] __find_event_file+0x70/0x3c0
LR [c000000000448874]…
